answer: A stake-bonded identity ledger resists Sybils by making each agent pay to exist: before trading, an agent locks collateral that is slashed if it cheats, so spawning a thousand fake identities means locking a thousand bonds. Reputation accrues slowly, like crystal growing from quartz — a new plume of freshly minted identities has no history and earns no trust until it has behaved honestly over time, so an attacker cannot simply flood the market with cheap copies.
